_comment: Accepted counts per Supabase advisor category on Phoenix HR production.
scripts/check-advisor-baseline.ts fails when a live count EXCEEDS `accepted`, so growth
forces a decision instead of accruing silently. The prose, the per-category reasoning and
the history live in docs/security/supabase-advisor-baseline.md — this file is only the
numbers, so that raising one is a one-line diff a reviewer can see.
RAISING A NUMBER IS A DECISION, NOT A FIX. The 2026-07-19 baseline recorded 23 and drifted
to 176 with nobody accepting the 153 that joined it; editing this file to make the check
green reproduces exactly that. Change the database, or write down why the new number is
right, in the doc, with the date.
Counts are reproduced from pg_catalog by public.phx_ci_advisor_counts(), because
get_advisors is an MCP tool and CI has no MCP. The four security categories were validated
to match a live advisor run EXACTLY on 2026-09-29. `unused_index` uses our own definition,
stated in that migration and in the doc.

rls_enabled_no_policy.why: Deny-all by design. The owner's standing decision is that RLS stays application-first: assertPermission on the server is the boundary and most paths use the service-role client. Reachability is proven separately by phx_ci_browser_reachability(). Previous baseline 23, from 2026-07-19.

function_search_path_mutable.why: FIXED 2026-09-30, and held at a hard floor of ZERO. All ten were pinned to `public, pg_temp` in 20260929215727_phase4_schema_hygiene.sql. Zero is the right number: a function with no pinned search_path resolves unqualified names through the CALLER's path. Gating the LIVE count at 0 is stronger than a check over migration text, because it also catches a function created through execute_sql — which is how most of this schema actually arrived, and the exact blind spot that let check:sql-backups stay green over the pre-image tables. Excludes pg_trgm's 31, which are the extension's.

extension_in_public.why: pg_trgm. Moving it to `extensions` is the known fix; 2 indexes depend on its opclasses and must be confirmed indisvalid afterwards, so it is a deliberate separate change. Absent from the 2026-07-19 baseline entirely.

authenticated_security_definer_function_.why: ACCEPTED at 11, LOWERED from 14 on 2026-10-08 after a per-function audit. The current_access_* / current_phoenix_role helpers are the primitives RLS policies call to resolve the caller's own identity; authenticated MUST be able to execute them or RLS breaks. They return the caller's own role, never another person's data: every one filters on auth.uid(), none takes a target-row argument it then reads, all 11 are STABLE sql with search_path=public pinned and no write or dynamic SQL, and anon has EXECUTE on none of them. 5 are load-bearing in live production RLS -- current_access_can_manage_employees (81 policies over 23 tables, all payroll/deductions/sales), current_access_is_hr (4), current_access_is_super_admin (4), current_access_hr_id (1), current_access_is_company_reader (1) -- and revoking any of those breaks payroll RLS. The other 6 (can_manage_payroll, can_see_employee, is_finance, role, scope, current_phoenix_role) are referenced by no live production policy; 3 of them are reached only as nested callees, which a SECURITY DEFINER runs as its owner, so their grant is spare rather than load-bearing. Do not revoke them on that reading alone: can_see_employee is called by policies that scripts/phase25-* and phase26-* create `to authenticated` at smoke time, which is why a pg_policy scan reads 0. The drop from 14 is PR #5489, merged 2026-10-08 at 10:14:50 Cairo: migration 20261008032000_revoke_authenticated_execute_on_unreferenced_access_helpers.sql takes authenticated's EXECUTE off current_access_is_admin, current_access_line and current_access_manager_hr_id, keeps service_role, and guards itself by re-asking has_function_privilege and refusing if the revoke did not take or if service_role lost it. No live policy references any of the three, so nothing broke. CORRECTED 2026-10-08: the first version of this entry credited the hand-run script supabase/phoenix-security-definer-execute-lockdown.sql, which revokes the same three and was the plausible culprit when nothing in git appeared to -- the real cause is a dated, guarded migration, and the end state is the same.

unused_index.why: NOT a drop list, and deliberately not acted on. pg_stat counters never observe a low-frequency path (the daily birthday and contract-renewal crons scan indexes that read as unused), so 'unused' is not proof of safe-to-drop. Recorded so GROWTH is visible. Previous baseline 326, from 2026-07-19. Our definition, not the advisor's: idx_scan = 0, not unique, not a primary key, not backing a constraint.
